outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the landscape of modern text-to-image generation, highlighting the limitations of current prompting techniques. It defines the two primary downstream tasks addressed in the paper—subject-driven and controllable generation—and establishes the critical challenges of finetuning large models without catastrophic forgetting.
subtopics: Overview of Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (Stable Diffusion, Imagen, etc.)
Limitations of Pure Text Guidance: Ambiguity and Lack of Fine-Grained Control
Defining Subject-Driven Generation: Identity Preservation with Few-Shot Learning
Defining Controllable Generation: Integrating External Signals (Edges, Segmentation)
The Core Challenge: Balancing Adaptability with Pretrained Knowledge Retention
Desiderata for Effective Finetuning: Efficiency vs. Generalizability Preservation

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Theoretical Foundations – Hyperspherical Energy and Semantic Structure
outline.description: Before diving into the method, this chapter builds the theoretical bridge between neural network geometry and semantic meaning. It explores why angular relationships between neurons are more critical than magnitudes for preserving generative semantics.
subtopics: Neuron Representation on Unit Hyperspheres
Hyperspherical Energy: Definition and Mathematical Formulation
Angular Information vs. Magnitude Information in Deep Networks
Evidence from Toy Experiments: Recovering Images from Angular Data Alone
The Role of Pairwise Neuron Angles in Encoding Semantic Knowledge
Why Euclidean Distance is Insufficient for Measuring Model Deviation

outline.description: This chapter details the core proposal of the paper. It explains how applying orthogonal transformations allows for model adaptation while mathematically guaranteeing the preservation of hyperspherical energy, thus maintaining the pretrained model's generative integrity.
subtopics: The Principle of Orthogonal Transformation in Weight Updates
Mathematical Proof: Preserving Hyperspherical Energy via Rotation/Reflection
Formulating OFT: Optimizing Layer-Shared Orthogonal Matrices ($\mathbf{R}$)
$\mathbf{W}_{new} = \mathbf{R}\mathbf{W}_{old}$: The Forward Pass Modification
Initialization Strategies: Ensuring Zero Initialization at Start ($\mathbf{R}=\mathbf{I}$)
Comparison with Standard Gradient Descent Finetuning

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Efficient Implementation and Variants of OFT
outline.description: This chapter addresses practical deployment concerns. It covers how to make orthogonal matrices computationally feasible through parameterization tricks like Cayley transforms and block-diagonal structures, and introduces advanced variants like COFT and Re-scaled OFT.
subtopics: Computational Challenges of Full Orthogonal Matrices ($O(d^2)$ Complexity)
Cayley Parameterization for Generating Skew-Symmetric Matrices
(Block-Diagonal) Block-Diagonal Parameterization for Reduced Parameters ($O(d^2/r)$)
